solver.kind: blind AI solver B (separate agent, answer-free packet, adversarial rubric)

R057-01.notes: B, C, D contradict the passage (house already sold; garden blooms as arranged; fences are background detail). 'Grasps why' slightly firmer than 'I thought I knew', but it is acceptable for a summary choice.

R057-02.notes: The white bulbs were placed where 'they would surprise people', and the mother reads them 'as if someone had left her a message'. D is ruled out by 'won't come up until April'. A fails because the house was already sold. B has no support.

R057-03.notes: The older narrator's ironic hindsight on being fourteen. C is the main trap, but nothing shows rudeness, only naivete.

R057-04.notes: Directly stated. A swaps the positions: red goes by the steps.

R057-05.notes: 'The polite thing to do' supports discretion. D is a weak literal trap.

R057-06.notes: 'Sleeping' plus 'said nothing to anyone' stress the hidden gift. A is contradicted: the tulips came up exactly as arranged. D: the white placement was deliberate.

R057-07.notes: Fading dusk light, so 'faint'. 'Watery' (as in 'thin, watery light') could tempt a few readers, but it carries a pale/diluted sense rather than dimming at dusk. 'Faint' is clearly best, so no flag.

R057-08.notes: C takes 'message' literally, a trap. Nothing supports B or D.

flags.note: Key nearly copies the last sentence ('come out smaller than it was'), so it can be matched by wording without interpretation. Also a small shift: the passage says the written-down REASON would come out smaller, while D says the GESTURE would seem smaller. It is still clearly the best answer, but consider paraphrasing, e.g. 'failed to capture the full meaning of what he had done.'

R057-09.notes: Close paraphrase of the final clause; A-C have no support.

flags.note: Wording: 'a neighbor recalling a time when the narrator was fourteen' is awkward because the neighbor IS the narrator. Better: 'a neighbor recalling a time when he or she was fourteen.' Not ambiguous.

R057-10.notes: First person, 'our street', 'my window', 'I was fourteen'. A, B, D are wrong.

R057-11.notes: 'A male who sees a flash at the wrong interval is likely to keep flying.' The passage never mentions brightness, so B and D are unsupported. C describes the normal case.
